validity.researcher_notes: This answers the length_ratio flag (drawn route 911 km vs LengthKnownKm 1,386 km, ratio 0.66). The VALUE is well corroborated, not the geometry. en.wikipedia.org's infobox independently states the SAME figure, '1,386 km (861 mi)', for this pipeline (verified https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dabhol%E2%80%93Bangalore_Natural_Gas_Pipeline, not sourced from GEM — its four footnotes are Jagranjosh/Economic Times/a GAIL press release/Infrastructure Today). The PNGRB register (already staged in the register-crosswalk leg) carries this authorisation at 1,414 km authorised, and its progression across editions (1,148 km commissioned per the 2025-06-30 edition → 1,182 km operating / 232 km under construction per the 2026-05-31 edition) shows 1,386 km sits between the register's currently-operating and fully-authorised figures — consistent with GEM having recorded the pipeline's announced/design total at its Dec-2013 commissioning (which is also what Wikipedia's four contemporaneous 2013 news citations describe) rather than the currently-still-partial operating extent. That reading matches the register-crosswalk's own VALIDITY flag on this row (concern_type classification, severity flag: 'GEM carries Dabhol-Bangalore as fully operating at 1,386 km, but the register still shows 232 km under construction... worth establishing whether the last 232 km was ever built or quietly dropped') — I am not re-litigating that value question, only confirming it from an independent angle. What IS new here: the drawn ROUTE is not a value problem but a geometry-completeness problem. Measured directly from data/individual-routes/gas-pipelines/P0915.geojson (haversine over each vertex pair): the main line runs Dabhol (73.158E,17.587N) toward Bangalore latitude in only 8 vertices, 761.8 km; a second line piece near the Konkan coast adds 130.3 km; a small Bangalore-approach piece adds 20.7 km; total ~912.8 km, matching the flagged 911 km. Eight vertices over ~760 km of hilly coastal terrain is a schematic-level trace (consistent with the route undershooting the true pipe length through the Western Ghats), even though RouteAccuracy is currently marked 'high' — that tag looks optimistic given the sparse vertex count, and is worth a look alongside the geometry redraw. I am not proposing new coordinates myself, per protocol.
